Slowing down the push rate seems to reduce the visibility of the flicker, but I would love to have it running as fast as possible on the board.

You can see more details around the investigation so far in Github issue #68.  You can also use entire to read the content of other agents' sessions or search for information in entire brain.  Session 4c516cba-60f9-4ecc-8569-06298f6abd52 is the most recent one that has been investigating. +# Unknown Pleasures flicker: independent review
+
+Rod, the evidence favours a problem associated with changing the picture,
+especially moving thin lines across pixels. It does not yet identify the
+physical mechanism. I would keep investigating before adopting speed 0.3 as
+the permanent solution: that slows the animation, and the existing evidence
+does not establish that normal-speed motion must flicker.
+
+Reviewed on 18 October 2026 at commit `86290b6`: issue #68 and its comments,
+Entire session `4c516cba-60f9-4ecc-8569-06298f6abd52`, scratchpad analysis
+scripts and data, application and installed M5GFX source, and the CO5300
+datasheet. Historical observations below come from Rod's recorded feedback
+and the prior session; new measurements are identified separately.
+
+## What survives an independent check
+
+I reanalysed the existing `g5864.raw` baseline video data, using a central
+300-by-300 crop and 12 horizontal bands. Across 22 selected update events:
+
+| Measurement | Mean ratio to settled image |
+| --- | --- |
+| Dimmest band | 0.863 |
+| Dimmest band versus the darker of old/new settled bands | 0.866 |
+| Whole central crop | 0.899 |
+| External mat reference patch | 0.998 |
+
+This reproduces the reported dip. Simply comparing an old frame with a
+brighter new frame does not account for it. Ordinary whole-camera exposure
+changes are also less convincing when the external reference stays steady.
+Rod's reports of visible flicker are independent evidence that the symptom
+is not solely a camera artefact.
+
+These are ratios of decoded camera values, not calibrated light output.
+The event detector selects minima, so this is a reproduction of the existing
+measurement, not an independent measurement of push timing. Rolling shutter,
+camera processing and the mixture of old/new spatial content remain relevant.
+The 14% figure describes the worst band, not uniform dimming of every pixel.
+
+## Conclusions I would push back on
+
+### The one-pixel shift does not rule out pixel-transition effects
+
+The probe shifts right, along the predominantly horizontal strokes in the
+native image. Moving every source pixel does not mean every destination
+pixel changes value: neighbouring points along a line often have similar
+values. Vertical motion crosses those strokes and is a different control.
+
+New measurements on the saved `up_a.raw`, with lit defined as decoded mean
+RGB greater than 40 out of 255:
+
+| Shift | Newly lit fraction of target lit pixels | Absolute intensity change / original total |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| One pixel horizontally | 19.78% | 0.592 |
+| One pixel vertically | 54.41% | 1.402 |
+
+These are illustrative measurements on one saved host image, not a capture
+of the exact frame in the device experiment. They nevertheless disprove the
+general reasoning that shifting the image changes every lit pixel's value.
+The issue's statement that the amount of pixel change is ruled out should
+be withdrawn.
+
+There is also a decoding trap: scratchpad `shift_probe.py` swaps the bytes
+again, whereas `dump_main.c` already writes ordinary little-endian RGB565.
+The measurements here decode that documented dump format without a swap.
+
+### Static traffic weakens one power hypothesis; it does not exclude power
+
+The near-static experiment is strong evidence against an unconditional
+blanking event on every full-frame write, or a dip caused only by the amount
+of bus traffic. It does not exclude transition-dependent panel current,
+transient supply behaviour, or effects that depend on the data pattern.
+
+Similarly, near-constant total brightness in completed host frames does not
+bound instantaneous current during a display update. Neither the time
+constant nor the transfer function of a hypothetical limiter was measured.
+Rejecting every APL/current-limit explanation because endpoint brightness
+changes by less than 1% is too strong. Those explanations are unproven, not
+eliminated.
+
+### The CO5300 register semantics matter
+
+The detailed CO5300 command description calls `0x55` **Auto Current Limit
+(ACL)**: `00` disables it and `11` enables it. Some generic-interface text in
+the same document calls it CABC, so the naming confusion is understandable.
+The existing `0x55 = 0` probe targets ACL, but acceptance was not verified.
+See the [CO5300 datasheet, printed page 190][datasheet].
+
+The installed M5GFX `Panel_CO5300.hpp` initialises `0x53` to `0x20`, which
+already leaves the documented DD dimming bit clear. The datasheet describes
+DD in connection with brightness-control changes; its existence is not
+evidence that normal RAM writes cause this dip. The
+[upstream initialisation][driver] matches the installed values.
+
+Crucially, installed `Panel_AMOLED.hpp` implements `readCommand()` and
+`readData()` as stubs returning zero. A zero read through those methods
+would prove nothing. Use a supported physical read path or a logic-analyser
+trace; a deliberate visible brightness change through the same command path
+can validate transport, but cannot alone prove ACL support.
+
+### Animation speed and push frequency are separate variables
+
+The recent `UP_SPEED` experiments reduce the hack's scrolling speed, not
+directly its refresh frequency. The source computes motion from elapsed
+time. At similar frame rates, speed 0.3 means smaller changes between images.
+That is different from slowing pushes while preserving animation speed.
+
+The sparse build changes geometry, render time, frame rate and image density
+together. It is encouraging, but cannot establish which variable helped.
+The fitted speed/dip line is useful interpolation over the tested points,
+not a physical law or a reliable extrapolation to other frame rates.
+
+## Most useful next experiments
+
+### 1. Replay two fixed frames with a stationary brightness reference
+
+Capture two consecutive device-rendered frames from the flickering build,
+then replay them without rendering. Preserve the current write path, TE
+offset and brightness. Include identical small grey and white reference
+patches at several screen heights, outside the moving scene but inside the
+written area. Start at the existing cadence.
+
+Compare `A A A A` with `A B A B`. Then hold each image for several pushes:
+`A A A A B B B B`. Log the actual flush start/end and frame identity. This
+separates content changes, repeated writes and rendering activity.
+
+- Only A/B transitions dip: investigate the changed pixel values and their
+  scan timing; repeated transport is insufficient to trigger it.
+- Unchanged reference patches dip too: a global or row-wide emission/current
+  effect becomes much more plausible.
+- References stay steady while moving strokes lose light: investigate
+  transition response and spatial scan effects before global brightness.
+- The replay is clean: return to rendering/presentation timing, actual
+  framebuffer contents and concurrent activity.
+
+Reference patches add some load. Keep them small, compare with and without
+them, and avoid changing the bounding box or push path accidentally.
+
+### 2. Repeat the shift control in both directions and both axes
+
+Use one static frame shifted by 1, 2 and 4 native pixels horizontally and
+vertically. Keep content inside a padded region so clipping does not change
+the total light. Record actual pixel-value turnover, not just the nominal
+translation distance. Try both directions relative to panel scanout.
+
+This tests a missing dimension of the existing control. Strong axis or
+direction dependence would favour scan/geometry interactions. Similar loss
+for comparable black-to-lit transitions on both axes would favour a pixel
+transition mechanism. Neither outcome alone proves the physical cause.
+
+### 3. Separate write cadence from motion per frame
+
+With the same A/B pair, vary the presentation interval while holding the
+images fixed. Separately, vary frame separation at a fixed presentation
+interval. This is cleaner than simultaneously changing density and speed.
+
+One particularly informative probe is to resend the new image after one
+panel refresh. If that shortens recovery compared with leaving the image
+alone, it suggests a missed/incomplete first update or another dependency
+on repeated writes. If recovery is unchanged, extra pushes are unlikely to
+help that mechanism.
+
+### 4. Measure light directly if the above remains ambiguous
+
+A photodiode and oscilloscope, with a GPIO marking the flush and TE captured
+alongside it, would distinguish optical emission loss from camera sampling.
+Measure a stationary reference patch and a region with moving lines. Check
+the relevant panel supply at the same time if practical; battery-versus-USB
+alone does not isolate the board's internal power rails.
+
+For another camera recording, lock exposure/focus/white balance, retain an
+external reference, and rotate the camera 90 degrees without changing the
+board. This changes the relationship between camera and panel scan axes.
+Use capture timestamps and the actual slow-motion segment when assigning
+milliseconds: the supplied MOV files declare a 30 fps playback stream.
+
+## What might be happening
+
+My leading family of explanations is a content-transition effect: newly
+lit portions of the moving strokes contribute less light during an update
+than their settled state, or scan timing produces a temporary spatial loss.
+Both fit the motion-speed dependence and survive the horizontal-shift test.
+The existing data does not distinguish them, and intrinsic OLED response
+time should not be assumed to explain a roughly 25 ms event.
+
+Current limiting or transient power behaviour remains possible but lower
+priority until unchanged reference pixels or rail measurements implicate it.
+Pure camera exposure variation and unconditional write-time blanking have
+substantially weaker support after the existing controls.
+
+For full-speed animation, increasing the rate of genuinely new frames is
+still a promising direction: elapsed-time motion then travels less distance
+per frame. Repeating the same frame more often does not reduce those jumps.
+If the loss follows changed pixels, optimising rendering may preserve the
+intended speed with less flicker. If it follows scan phase or global current,
+that needs a different remedy. Benchmark only after the replay isolates the
+relevant variable; do not adopt speed 0.3 as a root-cause fix.
+
+## Reproduction and limits
+
+The companion [audit script](issue68-audit.py) reproduces the new numbers:
+
+```sh
+uv run --with numpy python /private/tmp/issue68-audit.py \
+  /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-rod-build-stopwatch-screensaver/4c516cba-60f9-4ecc-8569-06298f6abd52/scratchpad
+```
+
+No firmware was changed, built or flashed, and no device experiment was
+performed in this review. No comments were posted to GitHub. The proposed
+mechanisms remain hypotheses. The local analysis and source checks establish
+the measurement reproduction and the limitations of the previous controls.
+
+[datasheet]: https://dl.espressif.com/AE/esp-iot-solution/CO5300_Datasheet_V0.00.pdf
+[driver]: https://github.com/m5stack/M5GFX/blob/master/src/lgfx/v1/panel/Panel_CO5300.hpp

Rod, **I’m satisfied the investigation has narrowed the problem considerably. I’m not satisfied that it has established the claimed mechanism or justified speed 0.3 as the final answer.** Stopping this particular overdrive implementation is reasonable.

The latest session output I retrieved ends with the second reviewer still running. I reviewed the preceding conclusions, probe code and analysis scripts.

The strongest new evidence is the vertical-shift experiment: moving strokes dim while unchanged grey reference patches stay steady. That makes a uniform whole-panel brightness reduction substantially less likely. The earlier horizontal-shift mistake has been addressed properly.

Three conclusions still need qualification:

- **“New pixels take 25 ms to brighten while old pixels vanish immediately” is only half tested.** The toggle analysis explicitly discards downward transitions. It measures rising responses but does not establish immediate turn-off. Analyse both directions before claiming that asymmetry explains the lost light. Camera exposure and temporal processing also remain part of the measured response.
- **The overdrive comparison changes more than brightness.** The first push waits for TE; the second calls `sinkAll()` directly, without another TE wait. See [the presentation code](/Users/rod/build/stopwatch-screensaver/firmware/src/main.cpp:658). It also changes cadence. A **100% gain, two-push control** is missing: that would distinguish effects of the extra write and its timing from effects of boosting pixels. The result establishes that this 120% implementation is unattractive—not that overdrive generally cannot work.
- **“The restore arrives late” is a hypothesis.** The analysis anchors events to brightness minima, rather than measured write times, and its supposedly quiet control windows sometimes contain large dips. The reported pulses are credible, but assigning each pulse to a particular stage needs better timing evidence.

I would **avoid another arbitrary 110% trial**. First analyse falling transitions in the existing clip. If pursuing overdrive further, run the 100% two-push control and measure both flushes.

More importantly, your original goal was lively animation without flicker. Speed 0.3 sacrifices roughly 70% of the intended scrolling speed; preserving frame rate does not remove that cost. Increasing the rate of genuinely new frames, while retaining normal animation speed, remains an untested route.

My recommendation: **record the current overdrive probe as unsuccessful, retain speed 0.3 as an optional mitigation, and leave the mechanism unresolved.** Wrapping up is reasonable as a deliberate effort-versus-benefit decision—but not as “we proved panel lag and exhausted the useful alternatives.”

+# Issue #68: recommended next steps after the second review
+
+Prepared for Rod and the investigating agent, 18 October 2026.
+Reviewed through the completed Fable hand-back and the parent agent's reply
+in session `4c516cba-60f9-4ecc-8569-06298f6abd52`.
+Source references below are at commit `ef0cf5c`.
+
+## Recommendation
+
+Continue with a bounded investigation aimed at preserving normal animation
+speed. Prefer the proposed 40-row, 50-point configuration over half-resolution
+rendering as the first candidate. Measure that same configuration both at its
+natural frame rate and capped to the baseline rate. This separates a useful
+rate comparison from the geometry change.
+
+First fix the analysis controls and extract falling responses from existing
+recordings. Do not spend the next flash on 110% overdrive or the proposed
+"restore on the next regular push" variant. Keep speed 0.3 as a fallback
+mitigation requiring Rod's acceptance of the slower animation.
+
+This handoff authorises no device writes or GitHub posts. Obtain Rod's
+approval where required by the repository workflow. No firmware was changed
+or flashed while preparing this review.
+
+## What is established, and what is not
+
+- The vertical-shift probe reproduces the dip while unchanged grey reference
+  patches remain steady. This strongly weakens uniform panel-wide dimming.
+- The completed reviewer and parent agent corrected the line-rendering claim:
+  Unknown Pleasures enables `GL_LINE_SMOOTH`; our TinyGL patch implements Wu
+  anti-aliasing. Grey-level and subpixel transitions remain relevant.
+- The parent independently measured limited overdrive headroom: effective
+  weighted boost about 1.146, not 1.20; approximately 7.9% of lit pixels
+  already have no headroom. This disqualifies the probe as a general verdict
+  on overdrive, while its performance cost still makes it unattractive.
+- The sparse result remains a useful unresolved observation. It changes
+  density, geometry and cadence together; it does not prove that 7 Hz itself
+  gives an additional factor-of-two improvement.
+- The reviewers' new numerical fits, pre-pulse and long-tail measurements
+  have not all been independently reproduced here. Audit their measurement
+  windows before promoting them to physical conclusions.
+
+Use wording such as: "Transition-dependent brightness loss, consistent with
+local display response; its dependence on cadence and scene geometry remains
+unresolved." Do not write "proved 25 ms LTPS hysteresis".
+
+## 1. Repair measurement controls before interpreting subtle effects
+
+### Concrete issue in the second review's null measurement
+
+In `scratchpad/review2/remeasure.py`, for periods below 30 camera frames:
+
+```python
+s0, s1 = int(P * 0.45), int(P * 0.85)
+ev2 = [e + int(P / 2) for e in ev ...]
+```
+
+The same statistic compares a window around each `ev2` with a reference
+window at `ev2 + s0` through `ev2 + s1`. At `P = 24`, the null centre is
+`e + 12`, but its reference is `e + 22:e + 32`, spanning the next event near
+`e + 24`. At `P = 16`, the reference is `e + 15:e + 21`, again spanning the
+next event. Thus the claimed no-event comparison can include an event in its
+denominator. A null near one does not demonstrate that the construction is
+valid, and subtracting it can bias comparisons across rates.
+
+Required changes:
+
+1. Identify each event's actual neighbouring updates, allowing timing jitter.
+1. Keep both numerator and reference windows inside demonstrably quiet
+   intervals, outside all transition/recovery intervals. If no quiet interval
+   exists, mark that event unsuitable for this null rather than forcing it.
+1. Plot the selected windows over several complete traces, including the
+   worst null outliers. Explain each exclusion rather than labelling it
+   "probably mis-anchored" and retaining the aggregate.
+1. Test the detector on synthetic constant signals, known dips at several
+   periods, and jittered events. Assert that no null window intersects an
+   injected event. Check recovery-window sensitivity explicitly.
+1. Report raw ratios, null distributions and any corrected statistic
+   separately. Do not mix worst-band, central-crop and full-disc measurements.
+
+The existing fold search also picks the strongest dip period and locally
+refines events to minima. That is useful for finding the phenomenon, but is
+not independent timing evidence. For subsequent device probes, log frame ID,
+TE timing and actual flush start/end; correlate with an optical marker if
+needed. Log every flush when a frame uses more than one.
+
+Do not claim a >100 ms response tail solely because the settled new image is
+1.4% below the old image. Different scene content can change the baseline.
+Use repeated identical transitions or toggle patches, and show within-state
+convergence towards the same plateau.
+
+### Extract both rising and falling toggle responses
+
+`scratchpad/analyse14.py` explicitly skips falling transitions with:
+
+```python
+if post - pre < 15:
+    continue
+```
+
+Therefore its table does not establish the claim that old pixels go dark
+immediately while new pixels brighten slowly. Analyse both directions in
+`IMG_5873.MOV`, separately for each patch and transition type. A normalisation
+of `(level - before) / (after - before)` works for either sign; reject small
+absolute swings, not negative swings.
+
+Show individual traces, event counts, median response and event-to-event
+spread. Estimate rise/fall times relative to their own stable endpoints;
+avoid combining patches until position-dependent scan timing is understood.
+Retain uncertainty from camera exposure, rolling shutter and processing.
+The low-amplitude C patches were already reported too noisy to support
+"every change lags".
+
+## 2. Run a normal-speed candidate with a matched-rate control
+
+Start with native 466-by-466 rendering and these three conditions:
+
+| Condition | Geometry | Animation speed | Cadence |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| A | Baseline 40 rows, 100 points | 1.0 | Natural baseline |
+| B | 40 rows, 50 points | 1.0 | Natural candidate |
+| C | Same as B | 1.0 | Capped to A's measured cadence |
+
+Important configuration detail: at this display size the upstream hack
+halves `MI_COUNT` in `reshape_unk` (`unknownpleasures.c:194-204`). Preserve
+the default count of 80 to obtain 40 rows. Override only `*resolution: 50`.
+Do not reuse `UP_SPARSE` unchanged: `registry.c:124-125` sets `*count: 40`
+as well, producing 20 rows. Verify the actual row count in a host dump.
+
+Keep brightness, line rendering, TE policy, write shape and overlays the
+same. Remove the copy/shift/reference/overdrive probes from this performance
+comparison unless deliberately included identically in all three builds.
+Retain full animation speed and confirm actual screen displacement over time.
+The hack uses elapsed time (`unknownpleasures.c:619-621`), so check that the
+cadence cap does not accidentally alter the animation clock or its tick logic.
+
+Before flashing, preview A and B at comparable simulated times and measure
+host cost. Follow the repository's native-test, build and copied-source
+verification requirements. Device measurements must report step time, copy
+and flush time, TE wait, and new-frame cadence separately. Do not assume
+halving points halves total rendering time.
+
+Interpretation:
+
+- B improves over C: higher new-frame cadence helps this same geometry,
+  including its smaller movement per frame. This does not distinguish those
+  two linked effects; that requires fixed-frame replay.
+- C improves over A: changed geometry/content helps even at matched cadence.
+- B looks good to Rod at normal speed: a practical mitigation is available
+  without proving the microscopic mechanism.
+- B remains too slow or visually poor: preview half-resolution rendering as
+  a separate candidate, not as an equivalent test of cadence alone.
+
+Half-resolution is a reasonable second candidate, but changes rasterisation,
+effective stroke width and pixel overlap as well as speed. The documented
+`glshim_set_render_scale(2)` setting is consumed by the next `glshim_open`
+(`.claude/rules/gl.md:277-281`). Scope any probe to this hack and restore the
+default for others. Keep vendor hack sources byte-identical.
+
+Record Rod's judgement of both motion and image quality. Prefer a repeated
+A/B comparison with neutral labels where practical. Do not impose a numeric
+visibility threshold inferred from the sparse-versus-speed-0.5 observations.
+
+## 3. Keep overdrive secondary, and correct the proposed redo
+
+There are three distinct limitations in the existing experiment:
+
+1. RGB565 clipping limits the boost, as the second reviewer established.
+1. The first push waits for TE; the nominal restore calls `sinkAll()` directly
+   (`main.cpp:640-645` and `658-662`). Its phase is not independently controlled.
+   This is a confound, not proof that the restore tears.
+1. It changes cadence and performs an extra full-frame write. A 100% gain
+   two-push control was never run.
+
+If this path is revisited, first compare one nominal push with two nominal
+pushes at the same scene-change cadence. Then compare 100% and boosted gain
+using identical timing, buffers and write paths. Measure both flushes rather
+than inferring their order from brightness minima.
+
+Do not accept "80% nominal, boost to 100%, restore next regular push" as an
+equivalent short overdrive pulse. At 5 new frames/s the next regular push is
+about 200 ms away, versus the proposed 25-30 ms transient. It can hold the
+boost roughly eight times too long, or replace the image before its own
+nominal restore. A new design must specify the per-pixel timeline and its
+refresh/copy budget. Dimming the nominal image also changes the comparison
+and needs its own no-overdrive baseline.
+
+The current result supports stopping this implementation. It does not show
+that all overdrive is ineffective, nor that gain 110% is the next useful test.
+
+## 4. Keep the mechanism hypothesis honest
+
+TFT hysteresis is a plausible named mechanism, supported by primary AMOLED
+research. One paper describes previous-image dependence and initial-frame
+luminance errors; another investigates delayed transitions and driver-level
+frame insertion. Neither identifies this board's mechanism. See
+[initial-frame luminance research][iflr] and
+[transition-response research][transition].
+
+Distinguish host writes/new images at about 5 Hz from the panel's internal
+scan refresh (previous TE measurements were about 60 Hz). Low-refresh-panel
+papers do not establish that repeated QSPI writes change internal TFT
+programming cadence. Nor do they establish that this controller has an
+accessible or inaccessible overdrive LUT. Do not assert either without
+controller/panel-specific evidence.
+
+The review's 13.5% "first principles" calculation is a plausibility estimate,
+not validation: A and B are defined by both starting and ending levels, not
+merely whether a target pixel exceeds brightness 200. A grey stroke turning
+on from black is not automatically a B-type dark-grey-to-mid-grey transition.
+Camera values are also not calibrated luminance. A predictive model would
+need a distribution of old/new pixel levels and measured response for those
+transitions, with scan and exposure timing accounted for.
+
+If distinguishing the physical mechanism becomes necessary, use a photodiode
+with TE/flush timing, or an independently characterised camera measurement.
+That need not block a good normal-speed mitigation accepted by Rod.
+
+## Deliverables and stopping decision
+
+Produce a short corrected evidence table with analysis provenance, then the
+A/B/C rate comparison and Rod's image-quality judgement. Draft corrections
+to the issue's anti-aliasing and overly certain mechanism claims; publish
+only with the applicable approval. Do not copy unsupported numbers into
+durable repository guidance.
+
+If a normal-speed candidate works, ship that focused change with the usual
+tests and device confirmation. If it does not, offer speed 0.3 explicitly as
+a slower-animation tradeoff. Close or defer the investigation by agreement,
+with the cause still labelled unresolved where appropriate. Do not present
+one failed candidate as exhaustion of all remaining possibilities.
+
+## Evidence locations
+
+- Entire session: `4c516cba-60f9-4ecc-8569-06298f6abd52`, completed Fable
+  hand-back and the following parent response.
+- Scratchpad root:
+  `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-rod-build-stopwatch-screensaver/4c516cba-60f9-4ecc-8569-06298f6abd52/scratchpad`.
+- Scripts: `analyse14.py`, `analyse15.py`, `trace_od.py`, and
+  `review2/remeasure.py`; recordings `IMG_5872.MOV` through `IMG_5874.MOV`.
+- AA implementation: `tools/tinygl_patch.py:110`; enabled by
+  `firmware/src/hacks/unknownpleasures/unknownpleasures.c:598`.
+- Overdrive headroom and restore path: `firmware/src/main.cpp:527-548` and
+  `658-662`; original TE wait at `640-645`.
+
+[iflr]: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12405611/
+[transition]: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44469-025-00002-5
*** End Patch"));
